After a 2022 lawsuit brought by York against Kittery 2024 was dismissed, the Council and Select Board agreed to a survey of metes and bounds which essentially reaffirmed the boundary in force for over 100 years with Kittery gaining approximately four acres of undevelopable land. The boundary that will be codified by this legislation satisfies both communities and their residents.

Testimony ofRepresentative Kristi Mathieson presenting

LD 2214, An Act to Confirm and Finalize the Boundary Between the

Town of Kittery and the Town of York

Before the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government

Good morning, Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury and members of the State and Local Government Committee. I am Kristi Mathieson representing House District 151, which is
Kittery. Thank you for your time today. It is my honor to present to you LD 2214, An Act to
Confirm and Finalize the Boundary Between the Town of Kittery and the Town of York.
For more than a century, Kittery and York have operated under a boundary line that differs from the vague and inconsistently mapped descriptions created in the 17th century. In 2019, York
raised concerns that the historic 1653 boundary did not align with the long-accepted modem line.
In response, both towns jointly funded a professional survey and engaged in several years of
negotiation to reach a mutually acceptable solution.
The municipalities have now agreed on a final boundary adjustment that transfers approximately
four acres of largely undeveloped land to Kittery. Both towns have formally approved identical resolve language and are jointly requesting legislative confirmation to provide final and legal
clarity for both communities.
In the First Regular Session of the 132nd Legislature, Senator Lawrence introduced LD 1196,
directing the towns to work together to resolve this issue. That bill was voted Ought Not to Pass in the State and Local Government Committee with the clear expectation that the municipalities
would collaborate independently. They have done exactly that, and LD 2214 reflects a
cooperative, good-faith resolution. I hope the committee will agree that this is the right moment
to bring this longstanding disagreement to a close. Both towns have invested significant effort in reaching a fair and mutually acceptable outcome. If the committee is willing, I also request adding an emergency preamble so the towns can benefit from this resolution as soon as possible.

Thank you for your time and thoughtful consideration.

District 151: Kittery
10061482:
Peter Joseph Representing: Town of York LD 2214
Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and Members of the Committee:
Thank you for taking the time to review LD 2214 "An Act to Confirm and Finalize the Boundary Between the Town of Kittery and the Town of York." As you may be aware, the exact location of the boundary between Maine's two oldest towns has been a somewhat contentious local issue for several years now. Although unfortunate, this dispute is not completely unexpected when dealing with a boundary shown on maps, descriptions, and land records which precede the creation of our nation and our state by a wide margin.
In late 2024, instead of continuing the debate of `how', `when', and `where' the observed municipal boundary has varied from the line originally described by colonial authorities, the municipal officers of both Towns agreed to make a good faith effort to formalize the boundary in its most recently observed location. To achieve these ends, the Towns jointly hired a licensed professional to survey the approximately 4.2 mile long boundary, and to develop both a plan view and a `metes and bounds' description of the currently observed boundary line. This work was completed over the summer and fall of last year.
Late last year, this boundary description was reviewed and endorsed by the York Selectboard, with the expressed purpose of submission to the Legislature to aid in the confirmation of the municipal boundary between the Town of York and the Town of Kittery. The Town of York respectfully requests the support of your Committee as well as the full Legislature on LD 2214, which we hope will finally resolve this outstanding matter. Representatives of the Town plan to attend your hearing on March 4th at 10:30am by video conference, and would be happy to provide any additional information or answer any questions that the Committee may have at that time.
Sincerely,
Peter E. Joseph Town Manager Town of York, Maine
